You are analyzing the Scotty3D codebase at /workspace (CMU 15-462 A2 halfedge mesh assignment).

ABSOLUTE RULE: You are READ-ONLY. Do NOT create, edit, write, or delete ANY file anywhere.
Do NOT run git commands that mutate state. Do NOT run the build. Only Read/Grep/Glob and
read-only bash (cat/grep/find/sed -n). Another agent is editing the source concurrently.

Key files to read:
- src/geometry/halfedge.h (element defs, invariants, API docs)
- src/geometry/halfedge-utility.cpp (interpolate_data, emplace_*/erase_*, validate(), Face/Vertex/Edge helpers, from_indexed_faces)
- src/geometry/halfedge-local.cpp (add_face example; stubs)
- src/geometry/halfedge-global.cpp (stubs)
- tests/a2/*.cpp (exact expected behavior)
- src/test.cpp (Test::differs for Halfedge_Mesh -- position/topology isomorphism)
- assignments/A2.md and assignments/A2/*.md (task specs)

The mesh invariants enforced by validate() are the ground truth for "valid mesh":
edge cycle exactly 2 halfedges; face cycle >= 3; vertex cycle >= 2; vertex has >=1
non-boundary face and <= 1 boundary face; edge has >= 1 non-boundary face; faces are
simple (no repeated vertex or edge); all data finite. Local ops must NOT call validate()
(complexity rules) -- they must pre-check instead.


TASK: Derive complete implementations of
  std::optional<Halfedge_Mesh::FaceRef> Halfedge_Mesh::extrude_face(FaceRef f)
  void Halfedge_Mesh::extrude_positions(FaceRef face, Vec3 move, float shrink)
in src/geometry/halfedge-local.cpp.

tests/a2/test.a2.l4.cpp is extremely specific. Extract EVERY constraint it imposes, including:
- extrude_face must return the SAME FaceRef (and same id) it was given;
- exactly deg(f) new vertices, 2*deg(f) new edges, deg(f) new faces; all new faces are quads;
- the new vertices must be the LAST deg(f) entries of mesh.vertices (the test walks backwards from
  --mesh.vertices.end()) and must be created at the ORIGINAL vertex positions;
- then extrude_positions(face, move, shrink) must produce the exact 'after' meshes for
  shrink=0.5/move=0, shrink=-1/move=0, and shrink=0/move=(0,0,1).
Derive from the third test whether 'move' is added directly as a translation vector.
Derive from the first two the exact shrink formula (lerp toward which centroid?) and note that
extrude_positions receives NO start positions, so it must recover the original ring positions by mesh
navigation from the inset face -- state exactly which navigation path yields them given your
extrude_face wiring, and confirm it is stable under repeated calls (the GUI calls it repeatedly with
absolute, not incremental, parameters: see src/gui/model.cpp around line 219).
Also handle: boundary face input (should it be rejected?), and what happens when f is a boundary loop.
Explain interpolate_data usage for all new vertices and halfedges.

Deliver complete C++ for both functions.

3	/*
4	 * Halfedge_Mesh
5	 *   Written By Keenan Crane for 15-462 Assignment 2.
6	 *   Updated by Max Slater for Fall 2020.
7	 *   Updated (extensively!) by Jim McCann for Fall 2022.
8	 *
9	 *  Represents an oriented, manifold 3D shape as a collection of vertices,
10	 *  halfedges, edges, and faces. Connectivity is pointer-based, allowing for
11	 *  many local operations to be done in constant time.
12	 *
13	 *  Here, manifold means that the neighborhood of every vertex is either
14	 *  equivalent to a disc (interior vertices) or a half-disc (boundary vertices).
15	 *
16	 *  Faces are oriented counterclockwise.
17	 *
18	 */
19	
20	#include <list>
21	#include <optional>
22	#include <set>
23	#include <string>
24	#include <variant>
25	#include <vector>
26	#include <unordered_map>
27	
28	#include "../lib/mathlib.h"
29	
30	class Indexed_Mesh;
31	
32	class Halfedge_Mesh {
33	public:
34		/*
35		 * A Halfedge_Mesh is comprised of four atomic element types:
36		 * vertices, edges, faces, and halfedges.
37		 */
38		class Vertex;
39		class Edge;
40		class Face;
41		class Halfedge;
42	
43		/*
44		 * Rather than using raw pointers to mesh elements, we store references
45		 * as iterators. For convenience, we give shorter names to these
46		 * iterators (e.g., EdgeRef instead of list<Edge>::iterator).
47		 */
48		using VertexRef = std::list<Vertex>::iterator;
49		using EdgeRef = std::list<Edge>::iterator;
50		using FaceRef = std::list<Face>::iterator;
51		using HalfedgeRef = std::list<Halfedge>::iterator;
52	
53		/* This is a special kind of reference that can refer to any of the four
54		   element types. */
55		using ElementRef = std::variant<VertexRef, EdgeRef, HalfedgeRef, FaceRef>;
56	
57		/*
58		    We also need "const" iterator types, for situations where a method takes
59		    a constant reference or pointer to a Halfedge_Mesh.  Since these types are
60		    used so frequently, we will use "CRef" as a shorthand abbreviation for
61		    "constant iterator."
62		*/
63		using VertexCRef = std::list<Vertex>::const_iterator;
64		using EdgeCRef = std::list<Edge>::const_iterator;
65		using FaceCRef = std::list<Face>::const_iterator;
66		using HalfedgeCRef = std::list<Halfedge>::const_iterator;
67		using ElementCRef = std::variant<VertexCRef, EdgeCRef, HalfedgeCRef, FaceCRef>;
68	
69		//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
70		// Local Edit Operations | src/geometry/halfedge-local.cpp
71		//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
72	
73		//if the result of an operation would cause the mesh to become invalid,
74		// it will instead not change the mesh and return std::nullopt.
75		//otherwise it returns the created/modified element (unless otherwise noted)
76	
77		//--- creation ---
78	
79		//create regular polygon face, disconnected from anything else
80		// (except an opposite-oriented boundary face required by validity)
81		// face is centered at (0,0,0), has normal (0,0,1), and has first edge pointing in the +x direction
82		std::optional< FaceRef > add_face(uint32_t sides, float radius);
83	
84	
85		//--- division ---
86	
87		//add a new vertex in the center of an edge
88		// (does not divide the adjacent faces)
89		std::optional<VertexRef> bisect_edge(EdgeRef e);
90	
91		//add a vertex at the midpoint of an edge and divide the adjacent non-boundary faces
92		// - the newly added vertex's halfedge should be aligned with the original edge
93		std::optional<VertexRef> split_edge(EdgeRef e);
94	
95		//put a vertex in the center of a face; divide f into a triangle fan around the new vertex
96		std::optional<VertexRef> inset_vertex(FaceRef f);
97	
98		//creates a face in place of a vertex, returning a reference to the new face
99		std::optional<FaceRef> bevel_vertex(VertexRef v);
100	
101		//creates a face in place of an edge, returning a reference to the new face
102		std::optional<FaceRef> bevel_edge(EdgeRef e);
103	
104		//inset a face into a face, return reference to the center face
105		std::optional<FaceRef> extrude_face(FaceRef f);
106	
107	
108		//--- modification ---
109	
110		//rotate non-boundary edge counter-clockwise
111		std::optional<EdgeRef> flip_edge(EdgeRef e);
112	
113		//turn a non-boundary face into a boundary face
114		std::optional<FaceRef> make_boundary(FaceRef f);
115	
116	
117		//--- unification ---
118	
119		//merge non-boundary faces incident to a given vertex, return the resulting face
120		std::optional<FaceRef> dissolve_vertex(VertexRef v);
121	
122		//merge faces incident on an edge, return the resulting face
123		// (merging with a boundary face makes the resulting face boundary)
124		std::optional<FaceRef> dissolve_edge(EdgeRef e);
125	
126		//remove an edge by collapsing it to a vertex at its midpoint
127		std::optional<VertexRef> collapse_edge(EdgeRef e);
128	
129		//remove a face by collapsing it to a vertex at its centroid
130		std::optional<VertexRef> collapse_face(FaceRef f);
131	
132		//weld two boundary edges together, returns first argument on success
133		std::optional<EdgeRef> weld_edges(EdgeRef e, EdgeRef e2);
134	
135	
136		//--- helpers ---
137	
138		//helpers used by the UI in conjunction with the above when doing beveling/extrusion operations
139	
140		//set vertex positions for a face created by beveling a vertex or edge
141		void bevel_positions(FaceRef face, std::vector<Vec3> const & start_positions, Vec3 direction, float distance);
142	
143		//set vertex positions for a face created by extruding a face
144		void extrude_positions(FaceRef face, Vec3 move, float shrink);
145	
146		//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
147		// Global Edit Operations | src/geometry/halfedge-global.cpp
148		//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
149	
150		//--- student-implemented methods ---
151	
152		//split all non-triangular non-boundary faces into triangles
153		void triangulate();
154	
155		//add new vertex at every face and edge center, without changing mesh shape
156		void linear_subdivide();
157	
158		//add new vertex at every face and edge center, applying Catmull-Clark-style position updates
159		void catmark_subdivide();
160	
161		//subdivide all non-boundary faces using the Loop subdivision rule.
162		// if any non-boundary face is a triangle, does nothing and returns false
163		// otherwise, returns true
164		bool loop_subdivide();
165	
166		//improve mesh quality via isotropic remeshing
167		struct Isotropic_Remesh_Parameters {
168			uint32_t outer_iterations = 3; //how many outer loops through the remeshing process to take
169			float longer_factor = 1.2f; //edges longer than longer_factor * target_length are split
170			float shorter_factor = 0.8f; //edges shorter than shorter_factor * target_length are collapsed
171			uint32_t smoothing_iterations = 10; //how many tangential smoothing iterations to run
172			float smoothing_step = 0.2f; //amount to interpolate vertex positions toward their centroid each smoothing step
173		};
174		void isotropic_remesh(Isotropic_Remesh_Parameters const &params);
175	
176		//collapse edges until no more than ratio * |edges| remain
177		// returns 'true' if it succeeds, 'false' if it ran out of collapse-able edges
178		bool simplify(float ratio);
179	
180		//--- provided methods ---
181	
182		//helper for Catmull-Clark-style subdivision.
183		// generates topology itself, assigns positions from parameters.
184		// used by linear_subdivide and catmark_subdivide.
185		void catmark_subdivide_helper(
186			std::unordered_map< VertexCRef, Vec3 > const &vertex_positions, //where to move current vertices after subdividing
187			std::unordered_map< EdgeCRef, Vec3 > const &edge_vertex_positions, //where to place the center-of-edge vertices
188			std::unordered_map< FaceCRef, Vec3 > const &face_vertex_positions //where to place the center-of-face vertices
189		);
190	
191		//re-orients every face in the mesh by flipping halfedge directions.
192		// no elements are created or erased; only Halfedge::next, Halfedge::vertex, and Vertex::halfedge pointers are changed.
193		void flip_orientation();
194	
195		//set corner normals:
196		// "smooth mode" (threshold >= 180.0f)
197		//   - all edges treated as smooth (even if 'sharp' flag is set)
198		// "auto mode" (0.0f < threshold < 180.0f)
199		//   - all edges with sharp flag are treated as sharp.
200		//   - all edges with angle (in degrees) > threshold are also treated as sharp.
201		// "flat mode" (threshold <= 0)
202		//   - all edges are treated as sharp
203		void set_corner_normals(float threshold = 30.0f);
204	
205		//set corner uvs per-face:
206		void set_corner_uvs_per_face();
207	
208		//set corner uvs by projection to a plane:
209		//  origin maps to (0,0)
210		//  origin + u_axis maps to (1,0)
211		//  origin + v_axis maps to (0,1)
212		void set_corner_uvs_project(Vec3 origin, Vec3 u_axis, Vec3 v_axis);
213	
214	
215		//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
216		// Element Definitions, Utility Functions | src/geometry/halfedge-utility.cpp
217		//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
218	
219		//--- mesh elements ---
220	
221		class Vertex {
222		public:
223			//connectivity:
224			HalfedgeRef halfedge; //some halfedge that starts at this vertex
225	
226			//data:
227			uint32_t id; //unique-within-the-mesh ID for this vertex
228			Vec3 position; //location of the vertex
229			//how much this vertex follows each bone's transform (used for skinned meshes):
230			struct Bone_Weight {
231				uint32_t bone;
232				float weight;
233			};
234			std::vector< Bone_Weight > bone_weights;
235	
236			//helpers:
237			bool on_boundary() const; //is vertex on a boundary loop?
238			uint32_t degree() const; //number of faces adjacent to the vertex, including boundary faces
239			Vec3 normal() const; //area-weighted normal vector at the vertex (excluding any boundary faces)
240			Vec3 neighborhood_center() const; //center of adjacent vertices
241			float angle_defect() const; //difference between sum of adjacent face angles and 2pi
242			float gaussian_curvature() const; //product of principle curvatures
243	
244		private:
245			Vertex(uint32_t id_) : id(id_) { }
246			friend class Halfedge_Mesh;
247		};
248	
249		class Edge {
250		public:
251			//connectivity:
252			HalfedgeRef halfedge; //one of the two halfedges adjacent to this edge
253	
254			//data:
255			uint32_t id; //unique-in-this-mesh id
256			bool sharp = false; //should this edge be considered sharp when computing shading normals?
257	
258			//helpers:
259			bool on_boundary() const; // Is edge on a boundary loop?
260			Vec3 center() const; // The midpoint of the edge
261			Vec3 normal() const; // The average of the face normals on either side of this edge
262			float length() const; // The length of the edge
263	
264		private:
265			Edge(uint32_t id_, bool sharp_) : id(id_), sharp(sharp_) { }
266			friend class Halfedge_Mesh;
267		};
268	
269		class Face {
270		public:
271			//connectivity:
272			HalfedgeRef halfedge; // some halfedge in this face
273	
274			//data:
275			uint32_t id; //unique-in-this-mesh id
276			bool boundary = false; //is this a boundary loop?
277	
278			//helpers:
279			Vec3 center() const; // centroid of this face
280			Vec3 normal() const; // area-weighted face normal
281			uint32_t degree() const; // number of vertices/edges in this face
282			float area() const; // area of this face
283	
284		private:
285			Face(uint32_t id_, bool boundary_) : id(id_), boundary(boundary_) { }
286			friend class Halfedge_Mesh;
287		};
288	
289		class Halfedge {
290		public:
291			//connectivity:
292			HalfedgeRef twin; //halfedge on the other side of edge
293			HalfedgeRef next; //next halfedge ccw around face
294			VertexRef vertex; //vertex this halfedge is leaving
295			EdgeRef edge; //edge this halfedge is half of
296			FaceRef face; //face this halfedge borders
297	
298			//data:
299			uint32_t id; //unique-in-this-mesh id
300			//both uvs and shading normals may be different for different faces that meet at the same vertex,
301			// so this data is stored on halfedges instead of (say) vertices:
302			Vec2 corner_uv = Vec2(0.0f, 0.0f); //uv coordinate for this corner of the face
303			Vec3 corner_normal = Vec3(0.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f); //shading normal for this corner of the face
304	
305			//helpers:
306			//convenience function for setting connectivity
307			void set_tnvef(HalfedgeRef twin_, HalfedgeRef next_, VertexRef vertex_, EdgeRef edge_, FaceRef face_) {
308				twin = twin_; next = next_; vertex = vertex_; edge = edge_; face = face_;
309			}
310	
311	
312		private:
313			Halfedge(uint32_t id_) : id(id_) { }
314			friend class Halfedge_Mesh;
315		};
316	
317		//--- data management ---
318		
319		//interpolate_data:
320		// sets the extra data on an element reference by mixing together data
321		// from a list of element references. Useful when merging, splitting,
322		// collapsing, or adding elements.
323		
324		// VertexRef version sets bone_weights:
325		static void interpolate_data(std::vector< VertexCRef > const &from, VertexRef to);
326		// HalfedgeRef version sets corner_uv and corner_normal:
327		static void interpolate_data(std::vector< HalfedgeCRef > const &from, HalfedgeRef to);
328	
329		/* interpolate_data usage examples:
330		  //TODO: change this and explain it a bit more
331	
332		  if adding a vertex vm on an edge with vertices (v1, v2), call:
333		    interpolate_data({v1, v2}, vm)
334		  if adding a vertex vm in a face with vertices (v1, ..., vN) call:
335		    interpolate_data({v1, ..., vN}, vm)
336		  if merging vertices (v1, ..., vN) to vertex vm call:
337		    interpolate_data({v1, ..., vN}, vm)
338	
339		  if dividing a halfedge h -> (h, h2), call:
340		    interpolate_data({h, h->next}, h2)
341		  if adding a halfedge h from the midpoint of a face with halfedges (h1, ..., hN) call:
342		    interpolate_data({h1, ..., hN}, h2)
343		  if merging halfedges (h1,h2) -> h call:
344		    interpolate_data({h1, h2}, h)
345		*/
346	
347		//--- memory management ---
348	
349		//use emplace_* to allocate new mesh elements:
350		// elements are added at the end of their respective list
351		// elements have a fresh id value and all references to other elements set to the end() of the appropriate list
352		VertexRef emplace_vertex();
353		EdgeRef emplace_edge(bool sharp = false);
354		FaceRef emplace_face(bool boundary = false);
355		HalfedgeRef emplace_halfedge();
356

358		// immediately clears the connectivity and data,
359		// sets the high-order bit of their id to 1,
360		// and adds to a free list for later reuse by emplace_*
361		void erase_vertex(VertexRef v);
362		void erase_edge(EdgeRef e);
363		void erase_face(FaceRef f);
364		void erase_halfedge(HalfedgeRef h);
365	
366		//elements are held in these lists:
367		//Don't add/erase elements from these lists directly!
368		// Use the emplace and erase functions above.
369		std::list<Vertex> vertices;
370		std::list<Edge> edges;
371		std::list<Face> faces;
372		std::list<Halfedge> halfedges;
373	
374		/* element lists usage example:
375	
376		  Visit every vertex in the mesh:
377		    for (VertexRef v = vertices.begin(); v != vertices.end(); ++v) {
378		        //do something for every vertex
379		    }

382		//--- misc stats ---

395		/// Check if half-edge mesh is valid:
396		// - all references held by elements are to members of the vertices, edges, faces, or halfedges lists
397		//   (no references to elements in other meshes, deleted elements, or past-the-end iterators)

38	/*
39	 * add_face: add a standalone face to the mesh
40	 *  sides: number of sides
41	 *  radius: distance from vertices to origin
42	 *
43	 * We provide this method as an example of how to make new halfedge mesh geometry.
44	 */
45	std::optional<Halfedge_Mesh::FaceRef> Halfedge_Mesh::add_face(uint32_t sides, float radius) {
46		//faces with fewer than three sides are invalid, so abort the operation:
47		if (sides < 3) return std::nullopt;
48	
49	
50		std::vector< VertexRef > face_vertices;
51		//In order to make the first edge point in the +x direction, first vertex should
52		// be at -90.0f - 0.5f * 360.0f / float(sides) degrees, so:
53		float const start_angle = (-0.25f - 0.5f / float(sides)) * 2.0f * PI_F;
54		for (uint32_t s = 0; s < sides; ++s) {
55			float angle = float(s) / float(sides) * 2.0f * PI_F + start_angle;
56			VertexRef v = emplace_vertex();
57			v->position = radius * Vec3(std::cos(angle), std::sin(angle), 0.0f);
58			face_vertices.emplace_back(v);
59		}
60	
61		assert(face_vertices.size() == sides);
62	
63		//assemble the rest of the mesh parts:
64		FaceRef face = emplace_face(false); //the face to return
65		FaceRef boundary = emplace_face(true); //the boundary loop around the face
66	
67		std::vector< HalfedgeRef > face_halfedges; //will use later to set ->next pointers
68	
69		for (uint32_t s = 0; s < sides; ++s) {
70			//will create elements for edge from a->b:
71			VertexRef a = face_vertices[s];
72			VertexRef b = face_vertices[(s+1)%sides];
73	
74			//h is the edge on face:
75			HalfedgeRef h = emplace_halfedge();
76			//t is the twin, lies on boundary:
77			HalfedgeRef t = emplace_halfedge();
78			//e is the edge corresponding to h,t:
79			EdgeRef e = emplace_edge(false); //false: non-sharp
80	
81			//set element data to something reasonable:
82			//(most ops will do this with interpolate_data(), but no data to interpolate here)
83			h->corner_uv = a->position.xy() / (2.0f * radius) + 0.5f;
84			h->corner_normal = Vec3(0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f);
85			t->corner_uv = b->position.xy() / (2.0f * radius) + 0.5f;
86			t->corner_normal = Vec3(0.0f, 0.0f,-1.0f);
87	
88			//thing -> halfedge pointers:
89			e->halfedge = h;
90			a->halfedge = h;
91			if (s == 0) face->halfedge = h;
92			if (s + 1 == sides) boundary->halfedge = t;
93	
94			//halfedge -> thing pointers (except 'next' -- will set that later)
95			h->twin = t;
96			h->vertex = a;
97			h->edge = e;
98			h->face = face;
99	
100			t->twin = h;
101			t->vertex = b;
102			t->edge = e;
103			t->face = boundary;
104	
105			face_halfedges.emplace_back(h);
106		}
107	
108		assert(face_halfedges.size() == sides);
109	
110		for (uint32_t s = 0; s < sides; ++s) {
111			face_halfedges[s]->next = face_halfedges[(s+1)%sides];
112			face_halfedges[(s+1)%sides]->twin->next = face_halfedges[s]->twin;
113		}
114	
115		return face;
116	}

### `A2L3` Collapse Edge Merge the two endpoints of an edge at the midpoint of the edge. Implementing these two functions will enable the `bevel face` (move a face in the direction of the normal and allow it to expand/shrink) and `extrude face` (move a face in the direction of the normal).
